items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: Willie Lewis's orchestra... Big Boy Goodie could swing... The musicians that were married took their wives with them... 'Big Boy Goodie' was a batchelor.

ctx.x: At the "Chez florence" there was never actually what you would call a show. There were entertainers, and they would have a singer. Apart from that we played dance music - a lot of it was just commercial orchestrations. Often, when I'd take my solo, I'd have to blow into my stand to keep it from being too loud. I always like to blow out, because it's difficult to play with the same intensity quietly. If you feel free to blow, it's easier to get the feeling. I had the same trouble in the Pump Room in Chicago with…

Looking back now, I think that Willie Lewis's orchestra must have been really quite good. It was quite a swinging band and had it been transported, for instance, to the Savoy, I think that Willie would have done as well as Teddy Hill, when he was there. Willie didn't have any big names but he had good musicians in the band. Big Boy Goodie could swing, and on a good night, Jack Butler could too. Billy Burns was not a great trombone player, but a lot of bands had trombone players who were not great jazzmen. The…

Jimmy Donaghue, Barbara Houtton's brother, also used to hang out with the orchestra. If we would go to a cafe after work, he would often come along. I don't know how interested in jazz he was, but he certainly seemed interested in the band.
